descriptions.text: It wasn’t just fireworks blowing up on New Year’s Eve... Orbit Chain’s Ethereum bridge lost $81.5M. What will 2024 bring?

The root cause is a combination of inadequate input validation in the "withdraw" function and flawed signature verification in the "_validate" function. These issues allowed the attacker to bypass access controls, manipulate withdrawal parameters, and execute unauthorized transfers Vulnerable code snippet: Attack transaction: https://bscscan.com/tx/0x1d0af3a963682748493f21bf9e955ce3a950bee5817401bf2486db7a0af104b4 Analysis: https://blog.solidityscan.com/orbit-chain-hack-analysis-b71c36a54a69

Cross-chain bridge protocol Orbit Chain has suffered an attack, resulting in a loss of $81.6 million. Orbit Chain has tweeted that the team has requested major cryptocurrency exchanges worldwide to freeze the stolen assets.

On December 31, 2023, attackers drained Orbit Bridge’s Ethereum vaults of approximately $81.5 million by compromising the multi-signature signing authority. The exploit did not involve a smart contract bug but instead bypassed the intended security threshold by controlling the majority of signing keys. Attackers obtained control over a majority (reported 7 of 10) of the Orbit Bridge Ethereum vault multisig signing keys, allowing them to authorize and execute withdrawals.
